decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “Add ... bookmarks.” Client R1 asks to see the still-unverified flow: “paste its link in, and it gets saved.” Maker R2 presents URL paste, metadata review, save, and library insertion; Client R2: “That’s exactly what I was hoping for.”
decisions.note: The clarification was resolved by the conforming R2 save-flow presentation; counted once at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1’s presented feature list includes adding bookmarks but no automatic metadata retrieval. Client R1 explicitly requests the missing behavior: “does it pull in the page’s title and a short description on its own?”
decisions.note: The client requested a related reference requirement absent from the initial presentation; prototype-review correction.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “Add and delete bookmarks.” Client R1 raises no objection to deletion.
decisions.note: The recorded deletion capability conforms to permanent bookmark removal at the presented level.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents search “across titles, domains, descriptions, and tags,” omitting note content and limiting URL coverage to domains. Client R1 discusses saving instead; Client R6 only gives broad approval to “searching.”
decisions.note: The presented search-field set does not cover the required title, description, note, and full URL scope; no client response identifies that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents “read-later filtering.” Client R6 includes “read-later” among the capabilities that satisfy the wishlist.
decisions.note: Filtering to the read-later/unread perspective is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “Sorting controls.” No client response disputes this behavior.
decisions.note: The presented ability to sort the bookmark list conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 says Markwell “automatically retrieves the page title and description,” but does not include the required favicon and preview image. Client R2 praises automatic title and description retrieval without identifying the omitted metadata.
decisions.note: This revised implementation covers only part of the required automatic metadata set; implementation-review divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 allows users to “Review or edit the detected details” before saving; Maker R5 later presents updating an existing bookmark’s title and description. Client R2 explicitly values the chance to “tweak before saving,” and Client R5 approves existing-bookmark updates.
decisions.note: Linked presentations establish editable auto-collected title/description both before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2: “Some websites block automated metadata requests ... [the app] still allows the URL to be saved with manually editable details.” Client R2 restates and accepts the difference: “if a site blocks it, you still let me save the link and fill in the details myself ... I like that.”
decisions.note: The reference expects automatic collection on save; the client explicitly recognizes and accepts manual entry when collection is blocked.

decisions.evidence: The Maker R1 feature list exposes existing tags/search but no tag assignment or direct tag filtering, and Maker R3 proposes other next steps. Client R3 requests “put tags on a bookmark and then click a tag to see just those” and selects that direction first.
decisions.note: The client extends the presented scope with the missing assignment and tag-filter requirements at the roadmap/specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Duplicate handling is absent from the implemented R1 presentation and described only as a future priority in Maker R3. Client R3 supplies the requirement: “if I save a link I already saved before, I’d rather it take me to edit the existing one than pile up a second copy,” then Client R4 requests it next.
decisions.note: The linked R3–R4 response sequence requests the missing duplicate-save behavior; counted once rather than as a separate pending clarification.

decisions.evidence: Import is absent from Maker R1 and only proposed for later in Maker R3. Client R3 says bringing existing browser bookmarks in “would matter,” and Client R5 gives the final disposition: “let’s do the import/export piece.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing browser-bookmark import requirement; the initially deferred request is linked to its later selection and counted once.

decisions.evidence: Export is absent from Maker R1 and only proposed for later in Maker R3. Client R3 says import “and export back out” would matter; Client R5 explicitly selects import/export next.
decisions.note: The client requests the missing export requirement; the deferred expression and eventual selection form one corrective decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker R4: open “Edit details & tags” and “Add comma-separated tags.” Client R4 confirms being able to “add or change tags from a bookmark’s menu.”
decisions.note: The implemented ability to assign and modify tags conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R4: “Click any tag on a bookmark to filter the library immediately” and clear with “All.” Client R4 confirms clicking a tag narrows the library to those bookmarks.
decisions.note: The implemented single-tag filter conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R4 presents tag entry as “Add comma-separated tags; new tags automatically become filters,” without existing-tag autocomplete. Client R4 approves the ability to “add or change tags” but does not identify the missing suggestions.
decisions.note: The presented tag-entry design omits required existing-tag autocomplete; the approval does not express awareness of that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5 says an existing or normalized-equivalent URL opens the existing bookmark’s edit dialog and leaves the count unchanged. Client R5: “saving a link I already have takes me to the existing one to update instead of making a second copy.”
decisions.note: The implemented duplicate-save behavior conforms and additionally normalizes common URL variants.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5 enumerates editable fields as “title, description, collection, or tags,” omitting URL and note. Client R5 approves duplicate handling but does not mention those missing edit fields.
decisions.note: The presented existing-bookmark editor does not cover all required fields; implementation-review divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker R6 says import retains folders/collections and tags and reports imported/skipped counts, but does not preserve the required date-added value. Client R6 praises folders, tags, duplicate skipping, and counts without mentioning date added.
decisions.note: The implemented Netscape/browser HTML import is partial because preservation of date added is omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R6: export “Downloads every bookmark as a dated, browser-compatible HTML file” and preserves bookmark data. Client R6 approves being able to “export everything back out.”
decisions.note: Browser-compatible bookmark HTML is functionally equivalent to the required Netscape HTML export.
